diagnosis.root_cause: mv_npu_top is effectively a stub with only parameter checks and no instantiated submodules or handshake/control logic. Therefore cmd_ready (and other interface outputs) are never driven per protocol/state, so no cmd transfer can occur and tests timeout waiting for cmd_ready.

first_divergence.expected: Asserted in IDLE to accept one command beat (subject to protocol/state)
first_divergence.observed: Remains non-asserted/undriven from reset through test wait window; send_beat times out

evidence.observation: SimTimeoutError at send_beat(... 'cmd_ready' ...) after max_wait; first failure at 1012ns.
evidence.relevance: Authoritative first functional failure is command handshake deadlock.

evidence.observation: Same SimTimeoutError waiting cmd_ready at job start.
evidence.relevance: Confirms systematic inability to accept command, not random data mismatch.

evidence.observation: Top contains only initial parameter assertions; no FSM/datapath module instantiations, no assignments for cmd_ready/vec_ready/mat_ready/bias_ready/out_valid/out_data/status_*.
evidence.relevance: Direct structural cause for missing protocol behavior and timeout.

evidence.observation: Requires ready/valid streaming command ingress and phased control progression from IDLE.
evidence.relevance: Establishes expected cmd_ready behavior and necessity of integrated control path.

repair_plan.recommended_change: Implement full top-level integration in mv_npu_top: instantiate mv_ctrl_fsm/mv_vec_buffer/mv_mac16_core/mv_postproc/mv_stream_if; generate all channel ready signals from FSM state and downstream readiness; generate xfer pulses strictly as ready&&valid; decode/store command via cmd_accept; route vector writes into buffer with proper address counter from FSM progress; unpack matrix beat to lanes and pair with vector lane chunk reads; drive compute/new_row sequencing and lane_valid_mask usage; connect row result into postproc with bias handshake and out backpressure support; expose status_busy/status_error from control. Ensure command ready is asserted in IDLE when able to accept a new job, and deasserted during active job per single-outstanding-job assumption.
do_not_change: Do not alter module interfaces or parameter contracts.
Do not modify frozen tests/reference behavior.
Do not change arithmetic semantics (INT8 signed multiply, INT32 wrap, optional bias/ReLU).
Do not change single-job ordering/backpressure protocol requirements.
expected_side_effects: Once integrated, failures may progress from handshake timeout to functional mismatches in compute/control sequencing if any submodule assumptions are inconsistent.
Ready/valid timing behavior becomes observable on all channels; regression may expose secondary protocol bugs.
